reason: This passage from Ezekiel 37 (the Valley of Dry Bones vision) contains only one explicitly named character: YHWH (יְהוָה), who appears throughout the text giving commands and making declarations. The prophet is addressed generically as 'ben-adam' (בֶן־אָדָם, 'son of man'), which is a form of address or appellative rather than a proper name. The spirit/wind (רוּח) is a force or entity but not a named character with agency. YHWH is unquestionably a leader - the ultimate authority figure issuing commands. No other named characters with proper names appear in this text.
